messages:
Maya P: Heads up — our Android sample app is hitting flaky socket reuse / EOF exceptions when the Retrofit client does token refresh under load. Seen on OkHttp 4.11 and 4.12.
Ben C: Ugh, same. Stacktrace looks like SocketTimeoutException / EOFException during reading response after a 401 -> refresh -> retry cycle.
Alex R: Are you using OkHttp's Authenticator to refresh, or a Retrofit Interceptor? Those have different concurrency semantics.
Maya P: We're using an Authenticator (synchronous) + an interceptor for attaching tokens. The bug reproduces when many coroutines cancel and new requests race for the refreshed token.
Sara L: Quick checklist: retryOnConnectionFailure, connection pool config, callTimeout vs readTimeout. Android's network flakiness magnifies race conditions.
Ben C: Tried disabling retryOnConnectionFailure and it reduced incidents but broke some legit transient retries.
Alex R: Can you paste the interceptor/authenticator snippet?
Maya P: Sure — here's a trimmed version from the sample app:

```kotlin
class TokenAuthenticator : Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    synchronized(this) {
      val newToken = TokenProvider.refresh() // blocks, network call
      return response.request.newBuilder()
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken")
        .build()
    }
  }
}

val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .build()
```

Maya P: The synchronized block prevents multiple parallel refreshes, but when coroutines cancel mid-request we still see connection reuse leading to EOF.
Sara L: OkHttp can reuse pooled connections even if the prior call was canceled; if a connection's socket is in a weird state the next call can hit EOF. We usually configure ConnectionPool and pingInterval for mobile.
Ben C: Proposed sample fix: set connectionPool with small idle timeout + set pingInterval for HTTP/2, and explicitly close connection on certain failures. Also consider calling response.close() in interceptors.
Alex R: For SDK parity note: Java sample had a different Authenticator implementation (using CompletableFuture) — add Kotlin-friendly sample showing coroutine-friendly token refresh + cooperative cancellation.
Maya P: Good call. Also we should document retry semantics: callTimeout vs readTimeout vs connectTimeout and when OkHttp retries. Many users expect Retrofit retry to mirror server SDK behavior but Android network is special.
Sara L: I'll draft a short doc blurb for the devportal: "Android: Handling token refresh and connection reuse" with code guidance (authenticator vs interceptor), recommended pool settings, and cancellation tips.
Maya P: I'll open a PR to the sample app to: 1) set ConnectionPool(5, 30, TimeUnit.SECONDS), 2) add pingInterval(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS) for HTTP/2, 3) show coroutine-aware TokenProvider that cancels refresh when coroutine job is cancelled, and 4) add a note about retryOnConnectionFailure tradeoffs.
DevExBot: CI checks queued for PR #482 (samples/android) — running unit + instrumentation tests. :gear:
Ben C: If CI passes, can we backport docs to the Java sample so parity stays intact?
Alex R: Yep — I'll mirror the Kotlin example in java/samples and add a short tests matrix for okhttp versions.
Maya P: Thanks everyone, will link the PR here once created.
